newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Zaire may still need military intervention - Canada.
newsitem.headline: Zaire may still need military intervention - Canada.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien said on Monday military intervention may still be needed to save hungry Rwandan refugees in eastern Zaire but that a force as small as 1,000 people could be enough.

"My view is we have to be ready for a military intervention. We are not sure how much of it is needed," Chretien told a news conference after a one-day summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum held in the Philippines.
Chretien said he discussed the Zaire question on the APEC sidelines with U.S. President Bill Clinton.
Referring to suggestions of a possible 10,000-strong multinational protection force for Zaire, Chretien said: "I don't think we need that much at the moment."
He added: "My judgement is we don't need 10,000 people. It might be more in the range of 1,000 or 1,500."

Chretien said military experts were investigating the possibilities of military intervention and added: "I know that many countries want to participate to help the delivery of humanitarian aid (in Zaire). Many countries are still very keen on that."

Western military leaders on Sunday met in Stuttgart, Germany, to discuss scenarios for helping refugees in Zaire that ranged from sending no new troops to using a multinational force to protect the refugees if necessary.

But they did not specify how many troops might be needed under any of the options, which must now go to political leaders for consideration. They also did not say where a mission could be based or what its rules of engagement might be.
